package generated

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"sync"

	machine "github.com/whitaker-io/machine/v4"
)

// The Go a .flow author writes beside their source. It is NOT generated; it
// stands in for the package the flow's references resolve into, so the golden
// file can be compiled AND RUN rather than only diffed.

type Order struct {
	ID   string
	Kind string
}

type Receipt struct {
	ID   string
	Seen int
}

func Poll() machine.EdgeFactory[Order] { return machine.Channel[Order](0) }

// done is closed once the sink has printed the token, so a host can exit on the
// datum arriving rather than on a timer.
var done = make(chan struct{})

var emitOnce sync.Once

// Done reports when a datum has reached the sink. It is what makes this golden
// RUNNABLE rather than only compilable: a host waits on it instead of sleeping.
func Done() <-chan struct{} { return done }

// Store is the sink, and it prints the LOCKED TOKEN from the fixture's own code.
// The assertion is on the running program's stdout, so nothing but the flow
// actually carrying a datum through Bill to the sink can produce it, and the
// count it prints is the one Bill wrote through the heap cell.
func Store(f machine.Frame[Receipt]) Receipt {
	v := f.Value()
	emitOnce.Do(func() {
		fmt.Printf("flow-golden: id=%s seen=%d\n", v.ID, v.Seen)
		close(done)
	})

	return v
}

// PageOnCall is the flow-level handler. A machine's error handler takes
// NodeError[any], which is why it is declared at that type.
//
// IT REPORTS, AND THAT IS LOAD-BEARING. The runtime's guard RECOVERS a node
// panic and hands it to dispatch, whose default is a silent drop, so a handler
// with an empty body turns a capability error or a nil dereference into a
// program that merely never finishes. Printing is what makes this fixture's
// failures readable at all.
func PageOnCall(err machine.NodeError[any]) {
	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "flow-golden: flow handler: node=%s panic=%t err=%v\n",
		err.Node, err.Panic, err.Err)
}

// NodeFailed is the node-level handler, whose type the runtime infers from the
// node it is attached to. It reports for the reason PageOnCall does, and it is
// the one that fires for the charge node: dispatch prefers the per-node handler
// and returns without consulting the flow-level one.
func NodeFailed(err machine.NodeError[Order]) {
	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "flow-golden: node handler: node=%s panic=%t err=%v\n",
		err.Node, err.Panic, err.Err)
}
